findings.title: Validator has a write side effect and runs on every validation
findings.body: BlockedEmail.should_block? increments match_count and saves the record each time it is called. The validator runs on every `valid?`, and users_controller#create calls `user.valid?` and then `user.save`, which validates again. A single signup attempt therefore bumps the counter twice, so the statistics are wrong. Validation should not write to the database.

findings.title: Email lookup is case-sensitive and unnormalized
findings.body: `where(email: email)` is an exact match. A blocked address can be bypassed by changing case (Bad@Spam.com) or adding whitespace. User emails are lowercased elsewhere via Email.downcase, but here neither the stored value nor the lookup is normalized.

findings.title: Racy read-modify-write counter increment
findings.body: `match_count += 1` followed by `save` is a lost-update race under concurrent signups. The save result is also ignored. An atomic `update_all` or `increment_counter` would avoid both problems.

findings.title: Nil value passed to validator and uses `and`
findings.body: The validator is applied with `if: :email_changed?` but a nil or blank email still reaches `value =~ regexp` and the BlockedEmail lookup. Using `and` instead of `&&` is also fragile. Add a blank guard, and note that `should_block?` can return nil, not just true or false.

findings.title: Shared array on controller prototype
findings.body: `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` is created once in the class definition, so every controller instance shares the same array. Rejected emails therefore persist across instances, and the array is never reset. It should be initialized in `init`.

findings.title: Failure response echoes user attributes
findings.body: The failure response now returns `errors` and `values` (name, username, email) back to the client. Combined with the client-side rejectedEmails logic, any email error, such as the uniqueness error, marks the email as rejected with the generic 'invalid' message. This hides the specific reason (taken, blocked, not allowed).
